sections.h2: Signs, trucks, mailboxes and gear: what outdoor-rated actually means
sections.html:
A sticker that lives outside has three ways to fail. The ink fades, the film shrinks and cracks, or the adhesive lets go at the edge and dirt creeps under. An outdoor sticker is built so none of those happen quickly: a thicker outdoor vinyl that stays flexible through heat and frost, a laminate with UV filtering over the ink, and a permanent acrylic adhesive that bonds harder as it ages. We print them in any shape, as singles, sheets or rolls, from a 2 inch equipment label to a 24 by 36 inch trailer panel.

The nearest sibling is our waterproof sticker. Waterproof means the material shrugs off water, soap and dishwashers, the right spec for bottles, coolers and bathroom products that mostly live indoors or in the shade. Outdoor means the whole assembly, film, ink, laminate and adhesive, is rated for direct sun and seasons of weather. If your sticker will be rained on but not sunbaked, the custom waterproof sticker page is the cheaper fit. If it is going on a yard sign, a truck door, a mailbox or a kayak that sits on a rack all summer, you are on the right page.

sections.h2: Sun does more damage than rain
sections.html:
Buyers worry about rain, but water rarely kills a laminated vinyl sticker. Ultraviolet light does. It breaks down the ink first, which is why reds and yellows go pale before anything else, then it embrittles the film. Here in Phoenix a bare printed sticker on a south-facing sign can look washed out in one summer. The laminate absorbs most of the UV before it reaches the ink and takes the abrasion from dust, car wash brushes and snow scrapers. Our outdoor vinyl is rated from -40°F to 176°F once applied, so a dashboard in July or a steel sign in a Minnesota January is within range.

sections.h2: Surfaces outdoor vinyl holds on, and the ones it will not
sections.html:
Permanent acrylic adhesive needs a smooth, clean, non-porous surface, and it reaches full bond after 24 to 72 hours.

  • Painted metal and factory auto paint: the best case. Wipe with isopropyl alcohol to remove wax and road film first.
  • Glass and acrylic: excellent grip; use clear vinyl if you want the glass to show through.
  • Powder-coated steel and aluminum: good, though a heavy texture lowers contact, so keep stickers under 6 inches on rough coatings.
  • Fiberglass, gelcoat and hard plastics: good on boats, trailers, coolers and cases; polyethylene needs a firm press and a full day to set.
  • Treated or painted wood: fine on smooth sealed boards, poor on raw or weathered lumber.
  • Stucco, brick, concrete block and canvas: avoid. The sticker grabs the high points only and lifts within a week.

Vehicles, windows, equipment and packaging each put different stress on a sticker, which is why we sort materials by job on our usage-based sticker categories rather than by material alone.

sections.h2: Applying outdoor stickers in heat, cold and wind
sections.html:
Most outdoor failures trace back to the first ten minutes: a dusty surface, direct sun at 105°F, or a January morning when the adhesive was too stiff to flow. Follow this order.

  1. Pick a day, or a spot in the shade, where the surface is between 50°F and 90°F. Move a vehicle into a garage if you can.
  2. Clean with isopropyl alcohol on a lint-free cloth and let it dry. Skip household glass cleaners and anything with wax or silicone.
  3. Peel the backing partway, line up one edge, and lay the sticker down from that edge with your thumb or a felt squeegee so air escapes ahead of it.
  4. Press the whole face firmly, then run a fingernail or squeegee around the perimeter. Edges are where water gets in.
  5. Leave it alone for 24 hours before rain or washing, and 72 hours before a pressure washer or an automatic car wash.

Small bubbles under laminated vinyl work out in a few days of sun; prick a large one with a pin and press it flat.

sections.h2: Sizes and artwork for reading at a distance
sections.html:
Indoors a sticker is read from arm's length; outside it is read from the sidewalk or the next lane. A rough rule is one inch of letter height for every ten feet of viewing distance, so a phone number meant to be read from 30 feet needs 3 inch digits. Keep to two or three lines, use a bold weight on a solid contrasting background, and leave 0.125 inch of bleed so the cut line never shows white. Thin outlines and type under 0.25 inch survive printing but not years of sun, so thicken them.

We cut outdoor stickers to any outline, as circles, rectangles, ovals or to the shape of your logo, from 0.5 inch up to 24 by 36 inches in one piece. Handout stickers for an event, the kind that end up on laptops and water bottles, do not need this heavier build and cost less on standard vinyl, which is what our custom promotional sticker page covers.

sections.h2: Ordering outdoor stickers and what arrives
sections.html:
Send a vector file (AI, EPS, SVG or PDF) or a 300 dpi PNG or JPG at final size and tell us the surface, the size and how many years you need. We will recommend white or clear vinyl, gloss or matte laminate, and permanent or removable adhesive, then send a free digital proof with the cut line marked. Prices start at $0.30 per sticker and depend on size, quantity and material; the minimum is 100 stickers per design. Production takes 5 to 7 business days after you approve the proof, delivery lands inside 8 to 10 business days, and FedEx shipping within the United States is free. Rush production is available if you give us the date.

Stickers ship flat up to 18 inches and rolled above that. Defective pieces are reprinted at no charge within our 10 day return window. The rest of the materials and formats we print are listed on the Die Cut Stickers home page.

faqs.q: How long do custom outdoor stickers last in direct sun?
faqs.a: Up to 5 years on a vertical surface such as a truck door, sign or window, with the laminate doing most of the work against UV. On a hood, roof or table top that faces the sun all day, expect 2 to 3 years before colors soften. Shaded spots last longer than any of those figures.

faqs.q: What is the difference between outdoor stickers and waterproof stickers?
faqs.a: Waterproof describes the material: vinyl or BOPP with a laminate, so water cannot soak it. Outdoor describes the whole build, which adds a thicker vinyl, a UV-filtering laminate and a permanent adhesive rated for sun, frost and heat. Every outdoor sticker is waterproof; not every waterproof sticker is rated for years of sun.

faqs.q: Do outdoor stickers need a laminate, or is UV-resistant ink enough?
faqs.a: They need the laminate. UV-stable ink slows fading but does nothing against abrasion from dust, brushes and scrapers, and it leaves the edge of the ink layer exposed to water. The laminate covers both problems at once, which is why it is standard on this product rather than an add-on.

faqs.q: Will outdoor vinyl stickers stay on a metal mailbox or sign through winter?
faqs.a: Yes, if they go on before the cold arrives. Apply between 50°F and 90°F, press the edges firmly, and give the adhesive 24 hours to set. Once bonded, the vinyl handles -40°F and ice without cracking. Applying in freezing weather is the mistake to avoid, since stiff adhesive never grabs properly.

faqs.q: Can outdoor decals go on stucco, brick or a textured wall?
faqs.a: No. Adhesive needs continuous contact, and a textured wall offers only the high points, so the sticker lifts within days no matter how good the vinyl is. For an outdoor wall, mount the sticker on a smooth aluminum or acrylic panel and fix the panel to the wall instead.

faqs.q: Which finish fades slower outdoors, gloss or matte?
faqs.a: They fade at about the same rate, since the UV filtering is in the laminate itself rather than the surface texture. Gloss shows colors deeper and sheds dirt a little better; matte hides scratches and avoids glare on a window or a sign read in low sun. Pick by looks and location.

faqs.q: Can I order outdoor stickers with removable adhesive for a seasonal sign?
faqs.a: Yes. Removable adhesive on outdoor vinyl holds through 1 to 2 years of weather and still peels cleanly from glass, painted metal and smooth plastic. It is the right choice for seasonal promotions, leased vehicles and rental equipment. For anything meant to stay five years, order permanent adhesive.

faqs.q: Are outdoor stickers suitable for boats, kayaks and jet skis?
faqs.a: Yes, on gelcoat, fiberglass and hard plastic above the waterline. Clean the surface with alcohol, apply dry, press hard and let the adhesive set for 72 hours before launching. Salt water is fine for the laminate; rinse the hull afterward so salt does not creep under the edges over a season.

faqs.q: How thick should an outdoor sticker be?
faqs.a: 3 mil vinyl plus laminate covers most flat surfaces. Move to 4 or 5 mil for bumpers, equipment and anything that gets handled or pressure washed, because the thicker film resists edge damage and conforms better over rivets and gentle curves. We recommend a thickness on the proof once we know the surface.

faqs.q: Can custom outdoor decals be printed on clear vinyl?
faqs.a: Yes. Clear outdoor vinyl with a UV laminate is the usual choice for storefront and vehicle windows, with a white ink layer printed behind light colors so they do not disappear. Expect 3 to 4 years outside rather than five, since the clear film has no white pigment helping block UV.

faqs.q: How many outdoor stickers do I have to order, and what do they cost?
faqs.a: The minimum is 100 stickers per design, and prices start at $0.30 per sticker. Size, quantity, vinyl thickness and a clear or reflective film all move the figure, so a quote with your dimensions gives the exact price. Larger runs bring the per-sticker cost down.

faqs.q: What temperature range do outdoor stickers handle once applied?
faqs.a: The vinyl and adhesive are rated from -40°F to 176°F in service, which covers a frozen trailer and a dark dashboard in a Phoenix July. The limit that matters more is application temperature: 50°F to 90°F on the surface itself. Outside that range the adhesive either will not flow or sets before you can position it.
